title: Auto-apply billing safety net for reserved-capacity burst claims (experiment)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers with reserved capacity occasionally hit short, predictable bursts (e.g., traffic spikes, sync jobs) that create small overage charges. These overage events often trigger manual invoice disputes and friction with account teams.

Goal: Run a controlled experiment that auto-applies a configurable safety-net credit to billing when an enterprise contract shows a short-duration reserved-capacity burst that is within the contract buffer policy. The feature should reduce manual dispute volume while preserving correct metering and auditability for finance and security questionnaires.

Scope: MVP applies to Dedicated and Private contracts with a defined "burst allowance" in the contract metadata. It will only auto-credit overage line items under configurable thresholds (e.g., <= 2% of committed monthly tokens or <= $500) and for burst windows <= 2 hours. Not in scope: self-serve hosted customers, post-invoice manual refunds, or changes to baseline metering collectors.
acceptance_criteria: Auto-credit rule is implemented server-side and configurable per org and per contract
Credits are recorded in the ledger with a link to the underlying request set and are visible on the invoice line items as separate adjustment entries
Auto-credit only applies when burst metrics fall within contract-defined thresholds (percentage, absolute $ cap, and time window)
Audit trail exported for finance includes request ids, model & route, time window, and rationale for credit
Feature guarded behind feature-flag and accessible via Console toggle and API contract metadata
No regressions in metering accuracy (<0.1% token accounting variance), verified by sampling tests
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal Redwood accounts + 2 pilot enterprise customers (manual opt-in). Duration: 2 weeks
Monitor: dispute volume, net ARR impact, false positives/negatives in crediting decisions
Beta: gradual opt-in cohort via Console for all enterprise orgs with Reserved capacity. Duration: 6 weeks
Full rollout: opt-out model after privacy/security sign-off and finance reconciliation script is stable
analytics_metrics: false_positive_rate (credits applied where contract didn't intend)
notes: Design constraints: invoice PDF/CSV must show adjustments clearly; finance requires exportable CSV with original metered amount and post-credit balance.
Legal/Contracts: Contract language needs an addendum for 'burst allowance' and auto-credit; PM to coordinate with Legal (PM-31700 dependency).
Security: exportable audit must be available for Security Questionnaire (SOC/ISO) review; security review requested -- ticket ENG-19821 is the implementation dependency.
Edge case: overlapping bursts across billing cycles — credits should be attributed to the cycle where the majority of tokens were consumed; decide deterministic tie-breaker (prefer earlier cycle).
Edge case: credits should not be applied if the same overage was the result of a client-side meter manipulation (we will mark as 'manual review required').
Experiment variant: A/B test variant B will apply credits automatically, variant A will surface suggested credits in Console for one-click approval by billing admin
